It was great to see Graham Adams back after illness and Ollie Foote defending his 5,000 metre title with gritty determination. Duane Hart looked good in the 400 while Gavin Teahan surprised with a classy 3,000 metre steeplechase.
A storming third leg by Graham Adams had brought us into third spot but in a scramble for the line Mike was gobbled up by three other teams including a fast moving Elliott Bunney.

Stuart Paton played a captain's role in 16th position, two places ahead of Marcello Bizio, and other notable runs came from Graham Adams, 23rd, Mark Sinclair, 32nd, and Jim Estall, 40th and making his debut for the Bels. on the country.
The most pleasing thing about the past season is the team spirit which has been generated by club captain Stuart Paton helped along by his brother Andy, also Graham Adams, Gary Staines and others.
Graham Adams gave us the good start we needed with his debut on a long stage - 25:37, writes Colin Pearson. Graham, better known for his audacious wit, is soon to be crowned the club's number 1.

Graham Adams was back home from the US for a short while and called in for Brandon Reid's farewell/Jackie Stone's 21st birthday party. Graham will be back to the states soon and then hopes to get to New Zealand and 'Oz'.

Fellow reveller Marcello Bizio similarly paid the price and having taken the lead in the steeplechase fell back dramatically at the end to be nearly caught by Graham Adams who won the 'B' race on his debut at the event.

Our Seniors, too, ran well, with Graham Adams leading the boys home. Roger Alsop might have been expected to have made the first ten but it's noticeable that on a course like this, with a narrow climb soon after the start, one has to commit one's self early.

All credit to Graham Adams. He shared the lead with the opposition for the first two laps of the Common but went away over the final 2.5 mile circuit for a clear win.

A fine win by Graham Adams, a welcome return to fitness and form by Jim Estall, and another solid performance by Phil Carstairs were the highlights of this third match in the Surrey league series.

Led by stars Gary Staines and Kassa Tadesse in 1st and 2nd places, both happy to run in spite of the heavy mud, then came our engine room boys, Jim Estall, Graham Adams, Roger Alsop and Phil Carstairs, fighting it out for the overall individual award and all finishing in the first eleven.

Graham Adams had it all his own way, cruising to a comfortable win while Charlie Dickinson, now well into his M45 age group, clocked a very pleasing best ever of exactly half an hour - pleasing, but what wouldn't he have given for a time just 1 second faster.
Swaying about on the back of the photographer's truck was Graham Adams, getting a grandstand view of his three team-mates as they mixed it with the world's best.

Heading out into the country again Matt Hillier was our fourth scorer ahead of Graham Adams. Matt fell on a slippery descent, but no sympathy came from our Captain who pointedly told him to, "get up and get on with it!"
Then came Graham Adams, Jim Estall, Roger Alsop, Phil Carstairs and Matt Hillier all fairly close and swapping positions throughout the race.
